topic: Land acquisition lapse under s.24(2), 2013 Act
argument_text: Following Pune Municipal Corporation and Sree Balaji, the acquisition proceedings must be declared lapsed on account of non-payment of compensation or non-taking of possession.
precedent_text: Resultantly, the decision rendered in Pune Municipal Corpn. is hereby overruled and all other decisions in which Pune Municipal Corpn. has been followed, are also overruled.

topic: Power-of-attorney holder's competence to depose (Order 3 Rule 2 CPC)
argument_text: The word 'act' appearing in Order 3 Rule 2 CPC takes within its sweep 'depose', so the provisions cannot be construed to disentitle the power-of-attorney holder to depose on behalf of his principal.
precedent_text: We are unable to agree with this view. The view taken in the case of Floriano Armando Luis cannot be said to have laid down a correct law and is accordingly overruled.
provenance: verbatim, both sides from the same chunk

topic: Whether civil court findings bind criminal courts
argument_text: It is a well-established principle of law that the decisions of the civil courts are binding on the criminal courts, but the converse is not true (Karam Chand Ganga Prasad v. Union of India).
precedent_text: This Court in Karam Chand Ganga Prasad v. Union of India, wherein it was categorically held that the decisions of the civil court will be binding on the criminal courts but the converse is not true, was overruled therein.
provenance: near-verbatim, quoted-within-quote structure -- worth a human sanity check

topic: Maintainability of a Consumer Protection Act complaint against a lawyer
argument_text: In respect of deficiency in service rendered by lawyers, a complaint under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 would be maintainable.
precedent_text: The view taken by the NCDRC to the effect that a complaint against a lawyer for deficiency in service is maintainable under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, is incorrect and stands overruled.
provenance: paraphrased from a single corpus sentence, split into the two propositions it states

topic: Whether title can be claimed automatically after limitation expiry (adverse possession)
argument_text: In view of the judgment in Gurdwara Sahib Vs. Gram Panchayat Village Sirthala, the petitioner cannot claim himself to be the owner automatically after the expiry of the limitation period.
precedent_text: The judgment of Gurdwara Sahib Vs. Gram Panchayat Village Sirthala has now been expressly overruled by a Three Judge Bench in Ravinder Kaur Grewal, which held that once the 12 years' period of adverse possession is over, even the owner's right to eject is extinguished.

topic: Enforceability of an insufficiently stamped arbitration agreement
argument_text: The Share Subscription Agreement, being insufficiently stamped, would be unenforceable in India.
precedent_text: The Supreme Court in In Re: Interplay Between Arbitration Agreements under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 has overruled the decision in NN Global.

topic: Permissibility of sub-classification within Scheduled Castes for reservation
argument_text: Sub-classification of the Scheduled Castes for the purpose of affirmative action is impermissible (E.V. Chinnaiah).
precedent_text: The holding in Chinnaiah that sub-classification of the Scheduled Castes is impermissible is overruled.

topic: Legislator immunity from prosecution for bribery related to a vote or speech
argument_text: A member of the legislature who has allegedly engaged in bribery for speaking or casting a vote is entitled to immunity from prosecution (PV Narasimha Rao).
precedent_text: The majority judgment in PV Narasimha Rao's case is not concurred with and is overruled.

topic: Applicability of s.97(1) CPC (Amendment) Act, 1976 to s.41 Punjab Courts Act
argument_text: Section 97(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 1976 has no application to Section 41 of the Punjab Courts Act (Kulwant Kaur v. Gurdial Singh Maan).
precedent_text: The Constitution Bench of this Court in Pankajakshi upheld the validity of Section 41 of the Punjab Courts Act, 1918, overruling this Court's earlier judgment in Kulwant Kaur & Ors. v. Gurdial Singh Maan.

topic: Validity of land acquisition urgency clause invocation
argument_text: The Division Bench in Shyoraj Singh was justified in applying the principles laid down in Radhy Shyam and quashing the acquisition proceedings.
precedent_text: Shyoraj Singh is set aside as it does not lay down good law and is per incuriam, having been passed overlooking the earlier precedents; Kamal Sharma lays down the correct proposition of law.
